story: A simple math error sparked a panic about black plastic kitchen utensils
text: Carbon steel pans are seasoned and generally will be stored with a light coat of oil. You'll add oil while cooking, as well. My carbon steel pans don't stick – an egg will happily glide on the surface. Stainless steel pans are not seasoned, but can still be relatively non-stick as long as they are heated properly prior to use. Heating them closes the pores in the pan's surface, making the surface smoother. Add oil after the pan is properly heated. This youtube video explains the process: [VIDEO]
This is how I cook them. It's pretty common knowledge for professional cooks[1], they just don't realize what it's called. [1] [VIDEO]
